speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: asked	the Minister for National Development in respect of the Home Improvement Programme (HIP) (a) what is the average time taken between polling to awarding a contract and to starting work; and (b) which precincts are experiencing the longest delay in implementing HIP to date since the programme started and how long has been the delay.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Upon the selection of HIP projects, HDB will call Design and Build tenders to procure contractors and consultants for the projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Once the tenders have been awarded, the contractors and consultants will work with HDB and the HIP Working Committees, which comprise representatives from the Town Council, grassroots leaders and residents, to design and work out the HIP package.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Residents are then consulted and engaged through straw polls before the formal HIP poll is conducted.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: In practice, the time taken for the HIP process differs from one HIP project to another and may not always fall within these general timeframes.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, progress of projects is dependent on technical constraints on the ground and site-specific issues, such as any affected underground services.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Projects where the design proposal is more complex, especially where it involves features, such as electrical upgrading works, can also take longer to complete.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I understand that it includes the upgrading of existing substations.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Would the Ministry consider, for example, letting the other part of the HIP proceed, the part where it involves very common kind of spalling concrete repair, replacement of pipes and casements?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Those are very common because I think a lot of residents are waiting for that.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Another question is: what is the purpose of the straw poll if HDB can proceed straight to the actual poll?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Are the votes gathered during the straw poll counted towards the actual poll?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I believe, in the Member's ward, there are two projects that are proceeding.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, these are issues that have to be undertaken because of the request of the Working Committee.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for whether the rest of the work can proceed whilst these things are being ironed out, when it comes to ESSes and where they are located, sometimes the residents may have a view on it and they may be reflected either in the straw poll or feedback that you get or during the actual poll, they may actually reject what you are trying to do.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: ESSes are buildings that may perhaps hinder some people's activities or their view or their ventilation, and these things have to be part and parcel of the design in order for all residents to make an informed choice when they decide to cast their vote for or against HIP.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A straw poll, as I have said earlier, gives the Working Committee and the HDB project team a sense of what the residents' concerns are.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As part of the poll, it gives you the indication as well, the Working Committee.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But if you feel that you want to do away with the straw poll, please let the Working Committee reflect that to HDB.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Does it mean that the votes gathered in straw polls are not counted?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: They have to do another poll, the actual poll?
